newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-TENDULKAR FACES ONE-DAYERS AND WINDIES WITH NEW HOPE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENDULKAR FACES ONE-DAYERS AND WINDIES WITH NEW HOPE.

text.p: India captain Sachin Tendulkar believes his team have revived their tour to South Africa despite being denied victory on the final day of the third test.
"I'm delighted with the team and proud of the way they have come back after the first two tests (which India lost by 328 and 282 runs).
"It was never going to be easy to make something of the series for ourselves but we did it and were very unlucky not to win the third test," Tendulkar said on Tuesday.
India take on West Indies in a five-test series in the Caribbean next month but before they leave South Africa they face their hosts and Zimbabwe in a triangular one-day series.
"We are now playing good, solid cricket and we can take that into the one-dayers. We have also been boosted by the arrival of four specialist one-day players who are fresh and keen to get started.
"Ajay Jadeja, Robin Singh, Salil Ankola and Sunil Joshican all win matches," Tendulkar said.

India were heavily criticised for two spineless batting performances during the first test in Durban when they were bowled out for 100 and 66. But Tendulkar's brilliant 169 in the second test in Cape Town lifted the side's morale.
"Rahul Dravid and Saurav Ganguly have developed tremendously on tour and have learned how to bat on quicker, bouncier wickets," he said.

"The West Indies series will be very hard but I don't think we have anything to be afraid of. You need to bat well in the West Indies, which we are now doing, and you need your fast bowlers to be in good form, which is certainly the case with Javagal Srinath and Venkatesh Prasad.
